newsitem.title: CROATIA: Insurance business expands in Croatia - paper.
newsitem.headline: Insurance business expands in Croatia - paper.

text.p: Insurance business in Croatia has expanding with inclusion of new services since the end of the war and privatisation of state-owned property, the Vjesnik daily reported on Monday.
Vjesnik, which published business results of all 15 insurers, said total premiums in the first six months reached 1.5 billion kuna, or 53.2 percent of last year's total.
The country's largest insurer, Croatia Osiguranje, has increased both its premium income and damage payouts, but its supremacy is on the market is slightly decreasing.

Its total market share shrank to 72.6 percent from last year's 77.1 percent despite higher premium insurance at 1.1 billion kuna. Preliminary profit of 23.5 million kuna was the highest in years, according to Vjesnik.
It put the share of two runner-ups -- Osiguranje Zagreb and Sava Osiguranje -- at five percent of the total premiums each.
Apart from motor liability and property insurance, life and health insurance are also on the increase, the paper said.
But it said the insurers were worried by increased damage payouts, especially in property insurance. Croatia alone paid out 19 million German marks in fire damages to two large companies.
